entities.name: Command R
entities.notes: CC-BY-NC license blocks production use without a separate Cohere commercial agreement

entities.name: DBRX
entities.notes: No updates since March 2024; largely superseded by Llama 3 and Qwen 2.5 class models

entities.name: DeepSeek
entities.notes: V3/R1 weight license is DeepSeek (not MIT); R1 distill variants are MIT; tool calling added in R1-0528

entities.name: Falcon
entities.notes: Falcon-180B uses TII Falcon License (non-Apache); Falcon 1 series limited to 2K context — effectively obsolete

entities.name: Gemma
entities.notes: Gemma 1–3 require license-acceptance gating; Gemma 4 is Apache 2.0 and ungated

entities.name: Granite
entities.notes: Tops out at 8B; explicit data provenance documentation makes it suitable for regulated industries

entities.name: Hermes
entities.notes: Fine-tune of Llama 3.1; inherits Llama 700M MAU cap; trained at 8K context so long-context quality may degrade

entities.name: Hunyuan
entities.notes: Proprietary Tencent license — not Apache 2.0; minimum 2× RTX 4090 even at Q4

entities.name: Llama
entities.notes: Broadest ecosystem support; community-license restricts apps over 700M MAU

entities.name: Mistral
entities.notes: Codestral v0.1 and Large-2407 are non-commercial; check license per variant

entities.name: Nemotron
entities.notes: Nemotron-4-340B has only 4K context; Llama-3.1-Nemotron-70B inherits 128K from Llama 3.1

entities.name: OLMo
entities.notes: Full pipeline open (weights + data + training code); English-only; 4K context is a hard limitation

entities.name: Phi
entities.notes: Phi-4 has only 16K native context; family is English-first despite some multilingual support

entities.name: Qwen
entities.notes: Qwen2.5 uses a proprietary Alibaba license; Qwen3 is Apache 2.0

entities.name: SmolLM
entities.notes: English-only; 135M/360M are too small for instruction following; designed for on-device edge deployment

entities.name: StarCoder2
entities.notes: Base model only — no instruction tuning; largely superseded by Qwen2.5-Coder and DeepSeekCoder-V2

entities.name: Yi
entities.notes: Largely superseded by Qwen3 and Llama 3 as of mid-2025; no native tool-calling format

entities.name: Aphrodite Engine
entities.notes: vLLM fork with broader quantization support (EXL2, GGUF, AQLM, BitNet); AGPL-3.0 has copyleft implications.

entities.name: ExLlamaV2
entities.notes: NVIDIA Ampere (sm_80) minimum; no OpenAI server built-in — TabbyAPI recommended for HTTP serving.

entities.name: gemma.cpp
entities.notes: Gemma-family only; CPU-only (no GPU); proprietary .sbs format with closed-source safetensors converter.

entities.name: Jan
entities.notes: Desktop chat app; GGUF-only for primary llama.cpp path; MLX backend added v0.7.7 for Apple Silicon.

entities.name: KoboldCpp
entities.notes: Single-binary llama.cpp wrapper with bundled browser UI for story/roleplay; AGPL-3.0 copyleft.

entities.name: llama.cpp
entities.notes: Upstream of Ollama, KoboldCpp, and llamafile; GGUF is the sole inference format.

entities.name: llamafile
entities.notes: Single-file portable executable via Cosmopolitan Libc; CUDA JIT is Linux-only (no CUDA on Windows as of v0.10.0).

entities.name: LM Studio
entities.notes: Closed-source, free-to-use; macOS supports Apple Silicon only (no Intel Mac).

entities.name: LocalAI
entities.notes: Multi-backend routing layer (36+ backends); also exposes Anthropic, Ollama, and ElevenLabs-compatible APIs.

entities.name: MLX / mlx-lm
entities.notes: Apple Silicon and macOS only; built-in server is not recommended for production.

entities.name: Ollama
entities.notes: Wraps llama.cpp; bundled CUDA libs — no separate toolkit install required.

entities.name: SGLang
entities.notes: macOS support is experimental (MLX backend, Python 3.11 only); Windows unsupported.

entities.name: Text Generation WebUI
entities.notes: Multi-backend web UI (~10 GB install); hot-swap between llama.cpp, ExLlamaV2, Transformers without restart.

entities.name: TGI
entities.notes: Now in maintenance mode; README redirects new projects to vLLM, SGLang, and llama.cpp.

entities.name: transformers
entities.notes: Library, not a server; GGUF loads as dequantized FP32 — for inference use llama.cpp or vLLM.

entities.name: vLLM
entities.notes: GGUF support is highly experimental; macOS via unsupported community plugin only.

entities.name: agno
entities.notes: Broadest provider coverage (30+); bidirectional MCP; AgentOS runtime exposes REST API with RBAC.

entities.name: Atomic Agents
entities.notes: Single-responsibility AtomicAgent components chained via Pydantic schema matching; built on Instructor.

entities.name: AutoGen
entities.notes: Now in maintenance mode; Microsoft recommends new projects use Microsoft Agent Framework.

entities.name: BeeAI
entities.notes: Dual Python+TypeScript SDKs; constraint-based RequirementAgent; Linux Foundation governance.

entities.name: CrewAI
entities.notes: YAML/Python hybrid config; LLM routing via LiteLLM (100+ providers).

entities.name: DSPy
entities.notes: Prompt-as-program paradigm; optimizer (MIPROv2, SIMBA) compiles typed Signatures into tuned prompts.

entities.name: Haystack Agents
entities.notes: Agents are Components in a Haystack Pipeline graph; MCP via Hayhooks companion tool.

entities.name: LangGraph
entities.notes: MCP via langchain-mcp-adapters; also available as a JS/TS npm package.

entities.name: Letta
entities.notes: Formerly MemGPT; requires a Letta Cloud or self-hosted server — no simple library mode.

entities.name: LlamaIndex Agents
entities.notes: MCP via llama-index-tools-mcp; strongest when paired with LlamaIndex's RAG and indexing ecosystem.

entities.name: mcp-agent
entities.notes: Low activity since early 2026; last commit January 25, 2026 — long-term maintenance uncertain.

entities.name: OpenAI Swarm
entities.notes: Superseded by the OpenAI Agents SDK; retained as an educational reference for the handoff pattern.

entities.name: Pydantic AI
entities.notes: Type-safe agent generics with FastAPI-style decorators; deep Logfire/OTel observability built in.

entities.name: Smolagents
entities.notes: CodeAgent emits Python as tool calls; sandbox (e2b/Docker) required in production.

entities.name: Aider
entities.notes: Git-native pair programmer; every edit committed automatically; no MCP support.

entities.name: AutoGPT
entities.notes: Pioneered autonomous agent loops; original MIT core largely superseded by Polyform-licensed platform.

entities.name: Continue
entities.notes: Repository archived 2026; final 2.0.0 release shipped; no further fixes will be accepted.

entities.name: Gemma Chat
entities.notes: Apple Silicon only; runs Gemma 4 via MLX locally; no API key required; model-specific.

entities.name: Gemma Gem
entities.notes: 930 stars 2026-06-14; runs Gemma 4 on-device via WebGPU; Chrome/Edge 113+ only; model-specific.

entities.name: Goose
entities.notes: Transferred from Block to Linux Foundation AAIF in 2026; 70+ extensions via MCP.

entities.name: GPT-Engineer
entities.notes: Archived April 22, 2026; historical precursor to lovable.dev; one-shot scaffold generation only.

entities.name: GSD-PI
entities.notes: 626 stars 2026-06-14; milestone/slice/task workflow with worktree-aware git automation.

entities.name: Mentat
entities.notes: Repo removed 2026-06-14; listed for historical reference only.

entities.name: Open Interpreter
entities.notes: Executes Python/JS/Shell locally; AGPL-3.0 limits commercial use; desktop app in early access.

entities.name: OpenClaw
entities.notes: Skills Registry (44,000+ skills); 22+ messaging channel interfaces; high-severity CVE history.

entities.name: OpenCode
entities.notes: Ships as both MCP server and MCP client; 75+ providers via built-in registry.

entities.name: OpenHands
entities.notes: Runs in sandboxed Docker; full browser + terminal environment; formerly OpenDevin.

entities.name: SWE-agent
entities.notes: Research-grade; active development shifted to mini-swe-agent; SWE-bench SOTA holder.

entities.name: Browser Control
entities.notes: Dominant implementation is Microsoft's playwright-mcp; supports HTTP transport via --port flag.

entities.name: Cloud APIs
entities.notes: Cloudflare's official server uses OAuth 2.1 with streamable HTTP; AWS/GCP community servers use stdio with ambient SDK credentials.

entities.name: Code Execution
entities.notes: E2B is the dominant cloud-sandboxed option and requires an API key; local Docker runners need no auth.

entities.name: Database
entities.notes: Auth is a database connection string/credentials, not a typical API key; read-only mode is the safe default.

entities.name: Git / GitHub
entities.notes: Local git server requires no auth; GitHub/GitLab servers require a personal access token.

entities.name: Memory
entities.notes: Reference implementation stores data in a local JSONL file; no multi-tenant isolation.

entities.name: Productivity
entities.notes: OAuth is the dominant auth pattern (Google, Notion, Microsoft 365); some providers use bot/API tokens instead.

entities.name: Shell
entities.notes: No Anthropic reference implementation; highest-risk MCP category due to arbitrary command execution.

entities.name: Web Search
entities.notes: All implementations require a paid third-party API key (Brave, Exa, Tavily, etc.).

entities.name: Chain-of-thought
entities.problem: LLMs jump directly to answers by pattern-matching, producing confidently wrong results on multi-step reasoning tasks

entities.name: Constrained decoding (JSON mode, grammar)
entities.notes: Requires access to token logits at inference time; not available via standard hosted chat-completion APIs without a structured-output wrapper
entities.problem: LLMs generate free-form text that may not conform to required schemas, causing downstream parse failures that require expensive retry logic

entities.name: Few-shot / in-context learning
entities.problem: Zero-shot prompts rely on the model's internal priors, producing inconsistent or off-format output for tasks with unusual schemas or domain conventions

entities.name: KV cache reuse
entities.notes: Automatic in production runtimes; agent developers benefit by keeping prompt prefixes stable
entities.problem: In multi-turn conversations and agentic loops, the model recomputes key-value attention tensors for unchanged prefix tokens on every request, wasting GPU compute

entities.name: Plan-and-execute
entities.problem: Step-by-step agents decide what to do next based only on the most recent observation, so they drift from the original goal on long tasks

entities.name: Prompt caching
entities.notes: Cache TTL is ~5 minutes on Anthropic; any prefix change causes a full cache miss
entities.problem: A large static system prompt sent on every request in an agentic loop is billed at full input-token rates, making high-frequency loops expensive

entities.name: RAG (retrieval-augmented generation)
entities.problem: LLMs have no access to private, domain-specific, or recently updated information beyond their training cutoff

entities.name: ReAct
entities.problem: An LLM acting in a loop has no mechanism to verify intermediate steps, so errors compound silently without real-world feedback

entities.name: Reflection
entities.problem: LLMs produce errors silently with no feedback loop, so the same mistake recurs and cannot be corrected within a session

entities.name: Self-consistency
entities.notes: Multiplies inference cost by N samples; only justified when accuracy is the top priority
entities.problem: A single chain-of-thought sample can follow a plausible but incorrect reasoning path and return a confident wrong answer

entities.name: Speculative decoding
entities.notes: Infrastructure concern; cannot be configured from a prompt or API call
entities.problem: Autoregressive decoding generates one token per full model forward pass, making large model generation slow and memory-bandwidth-bound

entities.name: Tool use / function calling
entities.problem: LLMs have a frozen knowledge cutoff and no mechanism to take actions or read live state, so they fabricate answers or refuse real-world tasks

entities.name: Tree-of-thought
entities.notes: Expensive in tokens and LLM calls; most production systems prefer simpler heuristics
entities.problem: Chain-of-thought reasoning is strictly linear, so a wrong turn early in a multi-step problem taints the entire chain with no way to backtrack
